what: sloped roofs hung open under the eave — outside views looked straight up into the roof's inner surface
cause: gableRoof/hipRoof/shedRoof build a one-triangle-thick shell (DoubleSide, no thickness). The slopes spring from the eave edge OUTSIDE the wall, so the whole overhang was open underneath: every oblique outside view showed the corrugated inner face of the roof. The hunting cabin had this closed by a hand-placed soffit block (33ca19b) but every other building still showed it — dark corrugated under the ranch porch, orange under the barn and church eaves.
fix: The soffit now lives inside the kit: gableRoof, hipRoof, and shedRoof each emit an eaveSoffit — a 6 cm horizontal lid at the eave plane spanning the full roof plan (walls + overhang). The slopes and the gable-end triangles all bottom out exactly at its top edge, so nothing pokes through and nothing z-fights. Every building with a sloped roof gets it at once: ranch main/ell hips, porch shed roofs, barn, bunkhouse, blacksmith, stamp mill, timber cabins, town gables (church, hotel), false-front sheds, hunting cabin. The cabin's hand-placed block was removed — it would have z-fought the kit lid on the same plane — and its roof passes soffitMaterial: dark to keep the approved wall-colour board; everything else defaults to the roof material.
